comments.author: midhatn
comments.body:
The ongoing work now has a canonical home in [Adaptive Inference](https://github.com/midhatn/adaptive-inference), with a [release](https://github.com/midhatn/adaptive-inference/releases/tag/v0.1.0) and an [evidence ledger](https://github.com/midhatn/adaptive-inference/blob/v0.1.0/docs/evidence.md). New development lives there as a portable gateway with bounded pending-request scheduling, timing feedback and optional engine/agent integrations.

The new gateway itself passed 45 software tests plus four reconstruction checks in all six Windows/Linux/macOS Python 3.11/3.12 CI jobs. A separate ready-backend run through the gateway completed eight exact-integer model answers and engaged learned timing for both gateway classes. The separately operated backend exited all six retained processes. Its first attempt after idle unload timed out under `reload_footprint_unavailable`; that failure and the narrower ready-backend acceptance are retained. Gateway classes are consumed by its own queue, so this is not a new native-priority or lease test.

The repository also publishes hash-checked source overlays for the earlier Strata/Hermes composition. Its predecessor Windows owner completed eight correct real-model requests, used three prior timing samples on each class's fourth request, and confirmed all eight retained process handles exited. Those historical results did not execute the new gateway; that owner itself is not shipped by these overlays.

This PR remains the scoped upstream memory-relief/lease draft. The downstream scheduler, #3399 composition, source-reconstruction checks and new gateway must retain their own identities and validation. This update does not mark the draft ready, transfer downstream results to its public head, or claim a speedup or universal memory safety.

<!-- adaptive-inference-publication-v0.1.0 -->
